questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane to see around other vehicles.
Ride close behind the vehicle in front of you to use their headlights.
Slow down to help you avoid hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help you avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid problems. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight.
Make eye contact with drivers.
Wave at drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when the engine runs. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: What happens if you drink one alcoholic drink before riding?

options.text: You cannot be convicted of DUI.
It will not affect your riding skills.
It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can make riding less safe. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows where the traffic lane ends on the right side.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Clothing that feels uncomfortable.
Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash, keep you comfortable, and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work well?

options.text: Fasten securely to your helmet.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow you to wear eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely to your helmet.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air flow to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you are in a separate lane.
Yes, because it blocks the wind.
No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. You could be in their blind spot, and the driver might move into your lane without seeing you.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from a person's body?

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: Why should you check your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To see if drivers behind you notice that you are stopping.
To watch for pedestrians in front of you.
To look for dark clouds that indicate bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if drivers behind you notice that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see if drivers behind you are paying attention to you. Use your mirrors when stopping to make sure drivers behind you are reacting to your stop.

questions.question: Which material gives the best crash protection?

options.text: Denim
Leather or synthetic materials
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials protect riders best in a crash. Wear long pants and jackets when riding.

questions.question: Which color makes you least visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green to be seen. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: Why is it hard to ride right after rain starts?

options.text: Other drivers may not react fast enough to the rain.
The road surface is extra slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road surface is extra slippery.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not washed away yet, mixing with water to create a slick surface.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.
Ignore them.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.
questions.explanation: Let tailgaters pass you. Going faster will only make them tailgate at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
The drinker's height
The outside temperature

questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means stop. Come to a complete stop and wait for a green arrow to turn.

questions.question: What should a rider's boots or shoes do?

options.text: Be below the ankles.
Cover the ankles.
Be made of soft material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, tough, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What should you do after riding over an object on the road?

options.text: Keep riding because the danger is over.
Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road. Check your tires and rims for damage and make sure nothing is stuck in the chain or belt.

questions.question: About footrests:

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them.
They are required for both driver and passenger.
They are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for both driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. This prevents your passenger from falling and taking you down with them.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go ahead with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist reduce the chance of a collision?

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road in front of the motorcycle.
Refuse to move to avoid potential hazards.
Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds down the road.
questions.explanation: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach the hazard.

questions.question: When must you wear goggles, impact-resistant glasses, or a helmet with a face shield?

options.text: You must wear them if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
They are optional if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
You must wear them if you are under 21 years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must wear them if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has no windshield, you must wear goggles, impact-resistant glasses, or a helmet with a face shield. A full-face helmet gives the best protection, even with a windshield.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: It improves your riding ability.
It does not change your riding ability.
It reduces your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your riding ability.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. If you drink any amount of alcohol, do not ride your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you first. This gives them the most time to notice you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: Is it safe to take over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: Yes, because over-the-counter medications are usually weak.
Yes, it is always acceptable.
No, medication may affect your riding ability and needs careful consideration.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, medication may affect your riding ability and needs careful consideration.
questions.explanation: Many legal medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can make it harder to ride safely. Ask your doctor how any new medication might affect your ability to drive or ride.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: They are less dangerous than using either one alone.
They balance each other out.
Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many medications can make riding unsafe. Some medications are even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What should good eye protection do?

options.text: It is not necessary if your motorcycle has a windshield.
It is only necessary during bad weather.
It should let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should let you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: California law requires proper eye and face protection. A face shield protects your face in a crash. Good eye protection must allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph. These include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When should you check your motorcycle for safety problems?

options.text: Before every ride.
Every week.
Once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle for safety problems before every ride. A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle is more dangerous than the same problem on a car.
